title: Confeature SDK wire-protocol fixture
description: Shared cross-SDK HTTP wire-protocol test cases (epic #146 sub-task B / issue #148 / spec 112). Each case describes one HTTP round-trip a SDK MUST conform to. The 58-tuple parity corpus tests evaluation semantics; this suite tests the wire layer (304/ETag/error classes/malformed body). Consumers live at apps/sdk-*/tests/wire/ and ingest this file at runtime — do not duplicate cases per language.

schemaVersion.description: Forced-touch gate for fixture format changes. Bump alongside every consumer. 1.1 (#336) adds optional given.baseUrl + expected.requestUrlPrefix for the custom-baseUrl case. 1.2 (#490) adds optional server.behavior (respond|timeout|close-mid-response) for transport-failure cases. 1.3 (#803) adds optional given.sdkKey + expected.requestPath — the exact parsed request path for a given key — and the rule that a consumer FAILS on an expected field it does not read.

errorClasses.description: Normalised error-class vocabulary that every SDK consumer maps its native error enum onto.

baseUrl.description: Optional non-default base URL the SDK is configured with for this case (custom-baseUrl case, #336). When absent the consumer uses its default test base URL. Pair with expected.requestUrlPrefix to assert the outgoing request honoured it.

sdkKey.description: Optional SDK key the SDK MUST be configured with for this case (1.3, #803). A `valid` key from sdk-key-shapes.json (enforced by scripts/validate-wire-cases.ts) — the one key list, never a per-SDK literal — except the one case the validator names (request-path-malformed-key), whose inline malformed key pins FR-001's one-segment url.PathEscape. When absent the consumer uses its own default test key. A consumer that ignores it while the case is present is a defect: the TS reader fails when the key it is handed differs.

behavior.description: How the mock transport acts (1.2, #490). 'respond' (default) delivers status+headers+body normally. 'timeout' never completes within the SDK's configured request budget — the SDK aborts and reports the timeout error class. 'close-mid-response' drops the connection partway through the body — the SDK reports fetchFailed (a transport failure, not parseFailed). When the field is ABSENT, consumers MUST treat it as 'respond' (JSON Schema `default` is advisory; the runtime default is the contract).

bodyRef.description: Reference to a sibling fixture file (e.g. config-v6.boolean.json) resolved by the consumer. Mutually exclusive with `body`.

body.description: Inline body bytes for cases that need malformed/non-JSON payloads. Mutually exclusive with `bodyRef`.

requestUrlPrefix.description: Optional assertion that the SDK's outgoing request URL starts with this string (custom-baseUrl case, #336). Verifies the SDK honoured given.baseUrl.

requestPath.description: Optional exact request path (1.3, #803). The consumer parses the recorded request URL, takes its path — still percent-encoded as sent, query string and fragment EXCLUDED — and compares it to this value with string equality (not a prefix, not a substring, not decoded). Requires given.sdkKey: the path is that key's path. FR-001: a well-shaped key travels raw, so for every valid corpus key this is /configuration-files/<sdkKey>/config_v6.json with the key's exact bytes — a ConfigCat-shaped key keeps its '/' as three segments, exactly a stock ConfigCat SDK's request; a malformed key is ONE segment escaped with Go's url.PathEscape. The query is excluded so the version carrier (#807) can add one without re-pinning.

allOf.comment: outcome=failed MUST set errorClass; outcome=fetched/notModified MUST NOT set errorClass.
outcome=failed implies hasConfig=false (no good config to surface).
outcome=notModified implies hasConfig=false (the 304 path does not re-emit the cached config — the caller keeps its own).
